speaker: Pat
text: Thanks for sitting down with us. Where would you like to start?

speaker: Sandy
text: Start? You can start by explaining why you are refusing to pay a bill for work you signed off on.

speaker: Riley
text: This is completely unreasonable. We did the work, the oak is in the building, and now you want a discount.

speaker: Pat
text: I understand this is frustrating. The amended bill is four hundred thousand over what we agreed.

speaker: Morgan
text: You agreed to it. Fawn approved the upgrade on your behalf like she has on every job for six years.

speaker: Jordan
text: Fawn was never authorized to approve a change of that size.

speaker: Sandy
text: Don't lecture us about authorization. You took a two-week vacation and left her running your business.

speaker: Riley
text: And then you come back and act like none of it happened. That is not how honest people operate.

speaker: Sam
text: I can see that you're angry, and I'm sorry we're in this situation. Tell me what's on your mind.

speaker: Sandy
text: What's on my mind is a one point four million dollar bill for oak that I have to pay in fifteen days.

speaker: Morgan
text: And a landlord who wants us bankrupt so he can keep the deposit and the space.

speaker: Pat
text: Nobody at this table wants you bankrupt. Help me understand the fifteen days.

speaker: Sandy
text: If the supplier isn't paid in fifteen days they stop shipping to every job I have. That's the business, gone.

speaker: Riley
text: Which you knew when you decided to stall on the invoice.

speaker: Jordan
text: We did not stall. We disputed four hundred thousand that was never in writing.

speaker: Sam
text: Can we take two minutes? I think everyone could use a breather.

speaker: Sandy
text: Fine. We're back. Say what you were going to say.

speaker: Pat
text: What I hear is that the supplier deadline is the real problem, more than the total. Is that right?

speaker: Sandy
text: Yes. If the supplier is paid, I can survive a fight about the rest.

speaker: Morgan
text: And we'd rather not fight at all. We want to keep working with you.

speaker: Pat
text: Then let's talk about what has to happen in the next fifteen days.

speaker: Jordan
text: We can release the one million we never disputed this week. The four hundred is the open question.

speaker: Riley
text: That gets the supplier paid. Why can't you release all of it?

speaker: Sam
text: Because the bank pulled our credit line last month. We are cash-tight for the quarter.

speaker: Sandy
text: I didn't know that.

speaker: Morgan
text: What if the remaining four hundred came out of future work instead of cash?

speaker: Pat
text: We have two projects starting in the spring. We could commit Sandy's crew to both.

speaker: Sandy
text: And the rent? I'm two months behind on the space.

speaker: Jordan
text: Fold it into the same schedule. Nothing due until the first spring project pays.

speaker: Riley
text: So: one million this week, four hundred against spring work, rent deferred. Did I get that right?

speaker: Pat
text: That's it. Let's write it down.
